findings: Request tags use a closed nine-tuple vocabulary and exclude path, literal edits, source, model and credential values.
Tags are derived only after native protocol validation and before peer/context admission; malformed frames stay unknown with no request hash.
Native admission and source effects remain in existing answer path; request attribution confers no authority.
Collector validates request-hash presence and successful page-kind consistency before stripping tags into existing bounded accounting.
The existing closed status/count/byte/session validators remain authoritative; aggregate vocabulary and request cardinality stay bounded.
Historical session schemas1-4 retain their prior accounting path and gain no fabricated operation attribution; mixed coverage is explicit.
New schema5 requires complete attribution and discovery fields.
Numerical broker hook is no-op by default; model-facing descriptor/request/response/guidance were not changed by this patch.
limitations: This is an independent source review, not a new Docker or live provider qualification.
Schema5 attribution is not present in the three frozen live trials; their historical refused-operation types remain unknown.
Aggregate accepted_requests counts accepted socket frames, not admitted source operations.
